question_text: A 3-year-old girl presents with her mother for a well-child checkup. Recent laboratory data has demonstrated a persistent normocytic anemia. Her mother denies any previous history of blood clots in her past, but she says that her mother has also had to be treated for pulmonary embolism in the recent past, and her brother has had to deal with anemia his entire life. The patient’s past medical history is noncontributory other than frequent middle ear infections. The vital signs upon arrival include: temperature, 36.7°C (98.0°F); blood pressure, 106/74 mm Hg; heart rate, 111/min and regular; and respiratory rate, 17/min. On physical examination, her pulses are bounding and fingernails are pale, but breath sounds remain clear. Oxygen saturation was initially 91% on room air and electrocardiogram (ECG) shows sinus tachycardia. The patient’s primary care physician orders a peripheral blood smear to further evaluate this finding, and preliminary results show a hemolytic anemia. Which of the following pathophysiologic mechanisms best describes sickle cell disease?

                    ### Question
                    A 3-year-old girl presents with her mother for a well-child checkup. Recent laboratory data has demonstrated a persistent normocytic anemia. Her mother denies any previous history of blood clots in her past, but she says that her mother has also had to be treated for pulmonary embolism in the recent past, and her brother has had to deal with anemia his entire life. The patient’s past medical history is noncontributory other than frequent middle ear infections. The vital signs upon arrival include: temperature, 36.7°C (98.0°F); blood pressure, 106/74 mm Hg; heart rate, 111/min and regular; and respiratory rate, 17/min. On physical examination, her pulses are bounding and fingernails are pale, but breath sounds remain clear. Oxygen saturation was initially 91% on room air and electrocardiogram (ECG) shows sinus tachycardia. The patient’s primary care physician orders a peripheral blood smear to further evaluate this finding, and preliminary results show a hemolytic anemia. Which of the following pathophysiologic mechanisms best describes sickle cell disease?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Increased red blood cell sensitivity to complement activation, making patients prone to thrombotic events
opb. An abnormality of the RBC membrane leading to morphological changes
opc. A recessive beta-globin mutation causing morphological changes to the RBC
opd. An X-linked recessive disease in which red blood cells are increasingly sensitive to oxidative stress
ope. Secondarily caused by EBV, mycoplasma, CLL, or rheumatoid disease

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Sickle cell disease is primarily caused by a recessive beta-globin mutation, leading to morphological changes in red blood cells and resulting in hemolytic anemia. The abnormality of the RBC membrane causing sickle-shaped RBCs is not the primary pathophysiologic mechanism in sickle cell disease. Relevant evidence supports the genetic basis and morphological changes associated with this condition.
